lines.japanese: 数字と記号と方程式にめくるめく長い五十分は過ぎた。
lines.english: A dizzying fifty minutes of numbers, symbols, and equations came to an end.

lines.japanese: チャイムが鳴った。
lines.english: The bell rang.

lines.japanese: そうするのが校則で定められているかのように、みんなが一斉に大きな息をついた。
lines.english: As though the school rules required it, everyone released a great breath at once.

lines.japanese: ひとコマ前の抑えたどよめきが、開放的な歓声に代わって教室を満たし、すぐにがたがたと椅子を引く騒音が続いた。
lines.english: The restrained murmur that had followed the previous exam gave way to open cheers that filled the classroom, followed at once by the clatter of chairs.

lines.japanese: 席を立った誰も彼もが、みな一様に他の机へ身を寄せあう。僕のひとつ前の席にも、ブランド大学に入ってコンパ三昧のキャンパスライフを目指している、おしゃれ系の男子グループが集まってきた。
lines.english: Everyone who rose immediately crowded around someone else’s desk. A fashionable group of boys who dreamed of entering prestigious universities and spending campus life at mixers gathered at the seat in front of mine.

lines.japanese: 引退するまでソラ学バスケ部の名ポイントガードを努めてきた鴻野君のお尻が、僕の机に引っかかってペンケースを踏みつぶしそうだった。
lines.english: Kono had been Misora’s star point guard until his retirement from the basketball club. Now his backside caught against my desk and threatened to crush my pencil case.

lines.japanese: 彼らは、帰りのショートホームルームが終わったあと、どこで昼食を取るかについて話しあっていた。
lines.english: They were discussing where to have lunch after the closing homeroom.

lines.japanese: 花水木通りの端の方に、値段は高めだけどウェイトレスのレベルも高い洋食屋があるとか、とくに最近入った巨乳の子が愛想ないくせに憎たらしいほどチョー可愛いとか、そんな話。
lines.english: There was a Western-style restaurant near one end of Flowering Dogwood Street, apparently—expensive, but with high-caliber waitstaff. The newest girl had enormous breasts and no charm whatsoever, yet was so cute it made you angry.

lines.japanese: おめーがガン見すっから俺ら全員が印象悪りぃんだよ、なんて言って鴻野君の硬い体が友人たちに小突かれるたび、僕の机も怯えるみたいにがたがた震えた。
lines.english: “You stare so hard, you make the rest of us look bad,” they told him. Every time his friends gave Kono’s solid frame a shove, my desk rattled as if it were scared.

lines.japanese: そうだ。僕は不意に思いついた。ホームルームが始まるまでにトイレを済ませておこう。
lines.english: Of course. A thought came to me. I would use the restroom before homeroom began.

lines.japanese: 僕は筆記用具をしまうと、音が立たないよう注意を払って椅子から離れた。
lines.english: I put away my writing things and slipped from my chair with care, making no sound.

lines.japanese: 教室の扉を小さく開けて、こっそりその隙間をすり抜ける。暖房の届いていない冷えた空気が頬に触れた。
lines.english: I opened the classroom door a crack and secretly slipped through. The unheated hallway air touched my cheek.

lines.japanese: とくに尿意なんてないと気付いたのは、ひと気のない廊下に踏みだしたあとだった。
lines.english: Only after stepping into the deserted corridor did I realize I had no need for the restroom at all.

lines.japanese: 廊下を斜めに横断して、ふらふらと隅の窓辺に寄った。
lines.english: I crossed the hall diagonally and drifted toward the window in the corner.

lines.japanese: 分厚いガラスの向こうには１２月の白い空が広がっているけど、危険防止措置が働いているため、僕らには窓を開けて手を伸ばすことが許されていない。
lines.english: December’s white sky spread beyond the thick glass. But safety measures denied us the right to open the window and reach out a hand.

lines.japanese: 遠い。
lines.english: Far away.

lines.japanese: 空が遠い。
lines.english: The sky was far away.

lines.japanese: 息が詰まる。
lines.english: I could not breathe.

lines.japanese: 目を閉じて、冷たいガラス窓に額を押しつけた。空きっ腹を舶来物のチョコレートバーでごまかしたような、落ちつかない胃もたれ感があった。
lines.english: I closed my eyes and pressed my forehead to the cold window. My stomach felt heavy and unsettled, as though I had tried to fool it out of its hunger with an imported chocolate bar.

lines.japanese: なんとなく横になりたいけど、保健室はＨ組のひとがよくいて落ちつかないから、最近はあまり行かないようにしている。
lines.english: I vaguely wanted to lie down. But people from Class H were often in the infirmary, which made it difficult to relax, so lately I tried not to go.

lines.japanese: Ｈ組……そうだ、森里君はもう来たかな……。
lines.english: Class H… That was right. I wondered if Morisato had arrived yet…

lines.japanese: また、ちょっと……見に行って、みようか……どうしよう……。
lines.english: Maybe I should… go and look again… Or perhaps not…

lines.japanese: 背後で音がした。誰か教室から出てきたみたいだ。
lines.english: A sound came from behind me. Someone seemed to have left the classroom.

lines.japanese: 不意に僕は、わけもなく居心地の悪さを感じた。なんでだろう。休み時間にひとりでいることは、べつに校則違反でもないのに。
lines.english: For no reason, I suddenly felt ill at ease. Why? Being alone between classes was hardly against school rules.

lines.japanese: 僕は路傍の石を気取るように、頭を前へもたせかけたまま動かなかった。さっさとトイレか森里君の教室に移動しておけばよかったと思う。
lines.english: Posing as a stone by the roadside, I kept my forehead bowed and did not move. I wished I had gone quickly to the restroom or Morisato’s classroom.

lines.japanese: 視覚を閉ざして鋭敏になっていた聴覚に、近付いてくる上履きの音が聞こえた──
lines.english: With my eyes closed, my sharpened hearing caught the sound of indoor shoes approaching—

lines.japanese: ──しかし、なぜだか足音は僕の後ろを通りすぎなかった。
lines.english: —but for some reason, the footsteps did not pass behind me.

lines.japanese: とん、とガラスを伝って、額にほんのかすかな振動を感じた。そして真横にひとの気配。
lines.english: Tap. A faint vibration traveled through the glass into my forehead. Then I sensed someone immediately beside me.

lines.japanese: 「これ面白いの？」
lines.english: “Is this fun?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 僕は目を開けて振りむいた。渡来さんが前傾姿勢でおでこを窓にくっつけていた。両腕が「小」の字みたいに小さく開いていた。
lines.english: I opened my eyes and turned. Watarai was leaning forward with her forehead against the window, her arms hanging a little way out from her sides.

lines.japanese: 「て、言うわけでもないみたいだね」
lines.english: “Apparently not.”

lines.japanese: 姿勢を直して僕の方を向く。
lines.english: She straightened and faced me.

lines.japanese: 「うん……まあ、面白くは……」
lines.english: “No… I can’t say it is…”

lines.japanese: いつものように、渡来さんはじっと正面を見据えて立っている。どうしてそんなにまっすぐな目で相手を見られるんだろう。
lines.english: As always, Watarai stood looking directly ahead. How could she look someone in the eyes with such perfect steadiness?

lines.japanese: 僕は元の場所へ視線を逃がした。どこまでも遠い空。至近距離で彼女の言葉を受けとめた窓ガラスは、わずかに白く曇っていた。
lines.english: My gaze escaped to its former place. The infinitely distant sky. The window that had received her words from inches away was faintly clouded.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、何してたの？」
lines.english: “Then what were you doing?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに……」
lines.english: “Nothing…”

lines.japanese: どぎまぎしながらガラス沿いに視点を上へ移す。渡来さんの白い吐息から、柳木原の白い空へ。
lines.english: Flustered, I moved my eyes upward along the glass, from Watarai’s white breath to the white sky over Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 「なんとなく……この窓、開けばいいのになあ、とか……」
lines.english: “I was just… thinking it would be nice if this window opened…”

lines.japanese: 「あー」
lines.english: “Oh.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは……変だよね、おれ」
lines.english: “Ah ha ha… I’m strange, aren’t I?”

lines.japanese: 「そういう日もある」
lines.english: “There are days like that.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは慰めるみたいな優しい笑顔で、しみじみと頷いた。
lines.english: Watarai nodded gravely, wearing a gentle smile that seemed to offer comfort.

lines.japanese: 「そう、どんなに寒くても……あ、暑い寒いは関係ないか、うん、外の空気を吸いたいときってあるもんね」
lines.english: “Yes. No matter how cold it is… Though I suppose hot or cold has nothing to do with it. Sometimes you just want to breathe the outside air.”

lines.japanese: 「良かった、分かってもらえて。なんだか機械換気って、空気入れかえてる実感薄いよね」
lines.english: “I’m glad you understand. Mechanical ventilation never really feels as though it’s changing the air, does it?”

lines.japanese: 僕は渡来さんの目を見たり見なかったりしながら言葉を続けた。
lines.english: I continued, meeting Watarai’s eyes and then avoiding them.

lines.japanese: 「やっぱりテスト終わったあとぐらい、窓を開けて思いっきり深呼吸したいし。ただでさえあの教室、なんかこもってるって言うか……ちょっと、息苦しいしさ……」
lines.english: “After an exam, especially, you want to open a window and take one enormous breath. That classroom already feels so stale… a little suffocating…”

lines.japanese: 「あ、だからだ？」
lines.english: “Oh. Is that why?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「いま羽田君、微妙に白い顔して席立ってったから、何事かと思って」
lines.english: “Your face looked a little pale when you got up just now. I wondered what was wrong.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 思いも寄らないことを言われて、僕は鏡代わりの窓に顔を近づけた。眼下に広がる柳木原の街並に、見慣れた男の面貌がうっすらと透けて重なる。その頬に手を添えながら尋ねた。
lines.english: The unexpected remark sent me closer to the window in search of a mirror. My familiar face floated faintly over the cityscape below. I touched my cheek and asked:

lines.japanese: 「そう……だった？」
lines.english: “Did I…?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。そう見えたよね」
lines.english: “Yes. That’s how you looked.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ……今も？」
lines.english: “Huh… Do I still?”
“Hmm…”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは前屈みになって、窓ガラスに映った僕の間抜けづらをじっと熟視した。どきりとした。さくらんぼみたいに顔がふたつ並ぶと、渡来さんの頭の小ささがやけに際立っていた。
lines.english: Watarai leaned forward and carefully studied my foolish reflection in the glass. My heart jumped. With our two faces side by side like a pair of cherries, the smallness of her head was striking.

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫。今はそうでもないみたい」
lines.english: “You’re fine. You don’t look especially pale now.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そう、良かった、はは」
lines.english: “Oh. Good. Ha ha.”

lines.japanese: ほの薄い鏡像が照れくさそうに笑った。照れくさそうで、楽しそうだった。自分のそんな顔を見るのは初めてだった。
lines.english: The pale reflection smiled bashfully. Bashfully, and happily. I had never seen that expression on my own face before.

lines.japanese: 「きゃは！　うっそ、なにそいつゲロムカだ！」
lines.english: “Ah ha! No way—god, that pisses me off!”

lines.japanese: そんな空気を入れかえるように、教室の扉が乱暴に開けはなたれた。クラスの女子がふたり、大きな声で笑いながら教室を出てくる。目が合いそうになって、僕はとっさに白い空を眺めた。
lines.english: As though to change the air between us, the classroom door flew violently open. Two girls emerged laughing at full volume. Our eyes nearly met, and I turned at once to the white sky.

lines.japanese: 何故だか急に声はやんだ。ガラス窓に映ったふたつのセーラー服が、渡来明日香と羽田鷹志という組み合わせを不思議そうに眺めている。
lines.english: For some reason, their voices abruptly ceased. Reflected in the window, two sailor uniforms regarded the combination of Asuka Watarai and Takashi Haneda with puzzled interest.

lines.japanese: 「あー岡村、この前言ったＣＤ持ってきたよ」
lines.english: “Oh, Okamura. I brought that CD I mentioned.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんの落ちついた声がきこえた。彼女が級友の苗字を呼び捨てるのは、ちょっと意外な気もしたし、妙にはまってる気もした。
lines.english: Watarai’s calm voice reached me. Hearing her address a classmate so familiarly surprised me a little. Somehow, it suited her.

lines.japanese: 「あ……ああマジで……ありがと……」
lines.english: “Oh… Seriously? Thanks…”

lines.japanese: 岡村さん（ていうらしいけど僕はその名前を覚えていなかった）は、ぎこちなく答えた。
lines.english: Okamura—apparently, though I had not remembered her name—answered stiffly.

lines.japanese: 「え……じゃあ、アレ？　いま、行く？」
lines.english: “So… are you coming now?”

lines.japanese: 岡村さんが渡来さんに問いかける。ぶつ切りの誘いはまるで暗号めいていて要点が見えない。僕の視界の隅で、渡来さんの長い髪が揺れた。
lines.english: Okamura addressed Watarai. The fragmentary invitation was too cryptic to reveal its point. At the edge of my vision, Watarai’s long hair stirred.

lines.japanese: 「んーん。ありがと、でも、まだ話終わってないから」
lines.english: “No. Thanks, but we’re not finished talking yet.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、お？　じゃあ、いいなら……あとで……」
lines.english: “Oh. Well, if that’s fine… later, then…”

lines.japanese: 足音が通りすぎていった。好奇心溢れるおしゃべりは再開されたみたいだけど、誰に遠慮してかボリュームはさっきより格段に小さくなっていた。
lines.english: Their footsteps passed away. Their curious chatter seemed to resume, but out of consideration for someone, its volume was drastically lower.

lines.japanese: 「岡村ぁー」
lines.english: “Okamura…”
“…What?”

lines.japanese: 窓から廊下に目を戻すと、渡来さんが右のこぶしを左のてのひらにぺちっと打ちあわせていた。
lines.english: When I turned from the window to the hallway, Watarai was smacking her right fist into her left palm.

lines.japanese: 「付きあってる、って言ってるのにもー。さすがに二年半も経つと信じない子も増えてきたよね」
lines.english: “I keep telling her we’re dating. After two and a half years, more and more people have stopped believing me.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ほら、いま聞いてたでしょ？　あの子、私が仲良くもない男子に話しかけられてうんざりしてると、よくああ言って、さりげなく連れだしてくれるの」
lines.english: “You heard her just now, right? Whenever some boy I’m not close to starts talking to me and I’m getting fed up, she says something like that and casually leads me away.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは遠ざかる背中を眺めながら腕を組んだ。
lines.english: Watarai folded her arms and watched the departing backs.

lines.japanese: 「そういう気配りはできる子なんだけどなあ。いかんせん他人の言葉より自分の思い込みに捕われすぎる傾向があるよね」
lines.english: “She can be thoughtful that way. Unfortunately, she has a tendency to trust her own assumptions far more than anything another person says.”
“I-I see…”

lines.japanese: 僕は渡来さんの視線を追って、そっと首だけ後ろへ回してみた。馴染みの薄いクラスメイトが、僕と同じようにこっちを窺っていた。
lines.english: I followed Watarai’s gaze, cautiously turning only my head. The classmate I barely knew was peering back at us in much the same way.

lines.japanese: 目が合ったら困るので、僕はまたすぐ正面に向きなおった。渡来さんは彼女たちに、涼しい笑顔で手をパクパクさせていた。
lines.english: Not wanting our eyes to meet, I immediately faced forward again. Watarai was opening and closing one hand at them, wearing a cool smile.

lines.japanese: 「あの渡来さん……それで、おれに話って？」
lines.english: “Um, Watarai… What did you want to talk to me about?”

lines.japanese: そうだ、いま彼女は級友に「まだ話終わってないから」と告げていた。それは何の話なんだろう。
lines.english: That was right. She had just told her classmate that we were not finished talking. What conversation did she mean?

lines.japanese: 「あ。うん。それなんだけど」
lines.english: “Oh. Right. About that.”

lines.japanese: ばいばいしていた渡来さんの手がぱくんと閉じられた。彼女は腕を下ろした。友人に向けていた笑顔もいっしょに消えた。
lines.english: Watarai’s waving hand closed with a snap. She lowered her arm, and the smile meant for her friend vanished with it.

lines.japanese: 彼女はまっすぐ僕の目を見ながら、一度口を開いて、またすぐ閉じた。唇を湿らせる。そしてふたたび口を開けた。
lines.english: Looking straight into my eyes, she opened her mouth once and immediately closed it. She moistened her lips. Then she opened it again.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、今日このあと空いてる？」
lines.english: “Haneda, are you free after this?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 一瞬、図々しい期待に胸が跳ねた。いや、まさか。僕は冷静を保った。そんな「まさか」があるはずない。
lines.english: For an instant, a shameless hope made my heart leap. No. Impossible. I kept myself calm. Nothing that impossible was going to happen.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、このあと？」
lines.english: “You mean… after this?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、放課後。もし良かったら、ちょっと付きあってもらいたいところがあって。どうかな」
lines.english: “Yes, after school. If you don’t mind, there’s somewhere I’d like you to come with me. What do you say?”

lines.japanese: まさかだ！
lines.english: The impossible had happened!

lines.japanese: 耳孔から入りこんだ甘い情動に体が熱くなる。胸は痛いぐらいにうずいた。僕は誘われている。渡来さんから誘われている。
lines.english: The sweet emotion entering through my ears set my body aflame. My chest ached with it. She was inviting me. Watarai was inviting me.

lines.japanese: まさかの悲願。残務処理の４番目。Ｗさんと遊びに行く。
lines.english: The impossible dream. The fourth item of unfinished business: “Go somewhere fun with W.”

lines.japanese: 「どう、どうってべつに……今日はまあ、たしか、わりと、暇な方だけど」
lines.english: “What do I say? I mean… I suppose I’m relatively free today.”

lines.japanese: 僕はちょっと俯き、おでこを掻くふりして手で顔を隠した。無意識の行動だったけど、きっと弛みそうになる表情を見られたくなかったんだろう。
lines.english: I lowered my head and hid my face behind one hand, pretending to scratch my forehead. The movement was unconscious, but I must not have wanted her to see the grin threatening to break across my face.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは息を短く吸って、ゆっくり吐いた。その息遣いが聴こえた。
lines.english: Watarai drew a short breath and slowly released it. I could hear her breathing.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、おっけ？」
lines.english: “Then we’re on?”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん……いいよ……」
lines.english: “Y-yes… That’s fine…”

lines.japanese: 沸きたつ血を抑え、僕は落ちついた振りをして答えた。しかし、いつまでも下を向いていては不自然だと気付き、あわてて顔を上げる。
lines.english: I subdued my boiling blood and answered with counterfeit calm. Then I realized that keeping my face lowered indefinitely would look strange and hurriedly raised it.

lines.japanese: 思ったとおり、渡来さんの揺るがない瞳はそこで待っていて、意思の強さを表すような唇はまっすぐに引き結ばれていた。
lines.english: As I expected, Watarai’s unwavering eyes waited there, her lips set in a straight line that seemed to express the strength of her will.

lines.japanese: そうだ、僕はなにを浮かれてるんだ、みっともない。彼女は意にも介してないじゃないか。
lines.english: That was right. What was I so excited about? It was pathetic. To her, this was nothing.

lines.japanese: 僕は自分の耳が赤くなってなければいいなと思った。
lines.english: I hoped my ears had not turned red.

lines.japanese: 「それで、どこに行くの？」
lines.english: “So where are we going?”

lines.japanese: こっそり深呼吸したあとで尋ねる。
lines.english: I asked after stealing a deep breath.

lines.japanese: 「うん。ゲーム屋さん？　て言うのかな。ゲームショップ？」
lines.english: “A game store, I think you call it? A game shop?”

lines.japanese: 「ゲームショップ……」
lines.english: “A game shop…”

lines.japanese: 意外な言葉が出てきた。
lines.english: The answer was unexpected.

lines.japanese: 「え、それはあの、クレーンゲームとかがある『ゲームセンター』じゃなくて？」
lines.english: “You mean a shop, right? Not an arcade with claw machines and things?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃなくて。ぴこぴこ売ってるとこ」
lines.english: “Not that. Somewhere that sells beep-boops.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは両手のこぶしをおなかの高さに上げて、それぞれの親指を立てたり引っこめたりした。真顔でそんなジェスチャーをする渡来さんに、ちょっと笑いがこぼれそうになった。
lines.english: Watarai raised both fists to stomach height and moved her thumbs up and down. Seeing her perform the gesture with a perfectly serious face nearly made me laugh.

lines.japanese: 「へえ……渡来さん、ゲームやるんだ？」
lines.english: “Huh… You play games, Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、あんまり」
lines.english: “No, not much.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は空想コントローラーをぴこぴこ操りながら首を横に振った。
lines.english: She shook her head while working the imaginary controller.

lines.japanese: 「だから、いろいろ教えてもらいながら見て回れればなーと思って。羽田君、ゲーム詳しいんでしょ？」
lines.english: “That’s why I thought I could look around while you explained things to me. You know a lot about games, don’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ……ううん、どうかな……」
lines.english: “What? No, I’m not sure…”

lines.japanese: 一年生のとき、ゲームセンターの格闘ものの対戦台で十連勝ぐらいしていたら、たまたまクラスの男子に遭遇したことがあった。
lines.english: In our first year, I happened to run into a boy from class after winning around ten straight matches at a head-to-head fighting-game cabinet in an arcade.

lines.japanese: 次の日あたりからしばらく僕はゲーム博士ともてはやされ、サッカー部の横田君や、校内での喫煙が三度発覚して去年退学になってしまった小森谷君あたりから、次々と大きな声の質問が飛ぶようになった。
lines.english: For a while after that, I was celebrated as the Game Professor. Loud questions came one after another from Yokota of the soccer club and Komoriya, who was expelled last year after being caught smoking at school for the third time.

lines.japanese: 僕がダンスビートエボリューションの上級ステップを実演したり、ささやきマテリアルの穂乃香シナリオを細かく紹介したりするたび彼らは歓声をあげ、僕の肩や背中や後頭部を叩いて喜んでいた。
lines.english: Whenever I demonstrated an advanced routine in *Dance Beat Evolution* or gave them a detailed account of Honoka’s route in *Whisper Material*, they cheered and struck my shoulders, my back, and the rear of my head in delight.

lines.japanese: でもある日、みんなの前で森里君が「てめえら、しょーもねえコトさせてんじゃねえよ」と凄んでから、あまり僕にその手の話題を持ちかけてくるひとはいなくなった。
lines.english: Then one day Morisato growled at them in front of everyone, “Quit making him do this stupid crap.” After that, few people brought those subjects to me.

lines.japanese: 「詳しいってほどじゃないよ。まあ……普通かな」
lines.english: “I wouldn’t say I know that much. I’m… about average.”

lines.japanese: あのころ森里君から「学校じゃそういうこと隠しとけ」と教わったので、僕は控えめに言った。
lines.english: Morisato had taught me back then that I should keep that sort of thing quiet at school, so I played it down.

lines.japanese: 実際プレイ本数自体は多い方じゃないと思う。でも、その手の情報はネットを巡ってるだけで自然に入ってくるから、本当は興味ないひとに比べればずっと詳しいんだろう。
lines.english: It was true that I hadn’t actually played all that many games. But simply roaming the internet brought that kind of information drifting in, so I was probably far better informed than someone with no interest at all.

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだー、んー」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは例の菩薩像みたいな微笑でうなずく。僕は咳払いをひとつした。
lines.english: Watarai nodded, wearing that same serene smile of a bodhisattva statue. I cleared my throat.

lines.japanese: 「でも、ゲームって言ってもいろいろあるよ」
lines.english: “But there are all kinds of games.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうみたいだね。でも──」
lines.english: “Oh, so there are. But—”

lines.japanese: 「そうだな。女の子だからやっぱりパズル系とか音ゲーかな」
lines.english: “Let’s see. You’re a girl, so maybe a puzzle game? Or a rhythm game?”
“Hm? Hmm?”

lines.japanese: 「ポップジャムミュージックとか、ゲーセンでよくうちの女子がやってるの見かけるよ。ほら、知らない？　こういう大型筐体でさ、こう、大きいボタンが九個付いてる……」
lines.english: “I see girls from our school playing things like *Pop Jam Music* at the arcade all the time. You know the one, don’t you? It has this big cabinet, and these—these nine huge buttons…”

lines.japanese: 「あ、でも音ゲーって初心者じゃ入りにくいのかな。最近の流行りだと、知能ゲーム系とか？　あの辺も人気あるよね。大人向けの触れ込みでＯＬにも受けがいいみたいだし、ほら、ＣＭでもさ──」
lines.english: “Though rhythm games might be hard for a beginner to break into. What’s popular lately… maybe one of those brain-training games? Those are pretty big too. They’re marketed to adults, and apparently they’re popular with women who work in offices. You know, even in the commercials—”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、得意な話題だと急に滑舌よくなるんだね」
lines.english: “Haneda, you suddenly get awfully articulate when the subject is one of your specialties.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　いや、べつに得意ってほどじゃないよ。うん、まあ、普通かな」
lines.english: “What? No, I wouldn’t call it a specialty. I’m… well, about average.”

lines.japanese: 「で、渡来さんが見たいのってどんなゲーム？」
lines.english: “So what kind of game did you want to see, Watarai?”

lines.japanese: 「ええとねー、なんだっけ。ちょっと、あるひとから聞いて興味持ったんだけど──」
lines.english: “Well, um… what was it again? Someone told me about it, and it sounded interesting, but—”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん、どんなのどんなの」
lines.english: “Mm-hm, mm-hm. What was it? What was it?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの……ちょっ、羽田君、近い近い」
lines.english: “Oh—um… Haneda, wait, you’re too close. Too close.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　ああ、ごめん、つい……」
lines.english: “What? Oh. Sorry. I got carried away…”

lines.japanese: 「羽田君、得意な話題だと急に積極的になるんだね」
lines.english: “Haneda, you suddenly get awfully forward when the subject is one of your specialties.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、べつに得意ってほどじゃないよ。まあ、普通かな。で、なんてゲーム？」
lines.english: “No, I wouldn’t call it a specialty. I’m… well, about average. Anyway, what game?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ、検索かけて調べたんだけど、名前忘れちゃったな…………あの、ほら、剣とか魔法とかで敵を倒して、なんかレベル？　を上げてく感じのやつで」
lines.english: “Oh, right—I looked it up, but I forgot the name… You know, the kind where you defeat enemies with swords and magic and raise your… levels? Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、ＲＰＧ」
lines.english: “Oh, an RPG.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはきょとんとして首を傾けた。
lines.english: Watarai tipped her head, looking utterly blank.

lines.japanese: 「んー、それじゃなくて、たしか……ろうぷれ？」
lines.english: “Hmm, no, that wasn’t it. I think it was… a role-playing game?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、だからＲＰＧだよね。定番ジャンルだから相当いろんなの出てるけど」
lines.english: “Right, that means RPG. It’s a standard genre, so there are an incredible number of them.”

lines.japanese: 「だよね。ちょっと見たんだけど、似たようなのたくさんあって途方に暮れちゃって。同じような名前でⅠとかⅡとか伝説とか冒険とか、も意味わかんない」
lines.english: “I know. I had a look, but there were so many that seemed exactly alike, I was completely lost. They all have the same kinds of names, with ones and twos and legends and adventures… None of it means anything to me.”

lines.japanese: 「分かった、任せて。店でパッケージ見ながら説明するよ。売れ線のものならある程度は把握してるから……あ、でもそれほど詳しくはないんだけどね。うん、まあ、普通かな」
lines.english: “All right, leave it to me. I’ll explain them while we look at the boxes in the store. I keep track of the big sellers, at least… Though I’m not really that knowledgeable. I’m, well, about average.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだー、んー」
lines.english: “Oh, I see. Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、でも、普通に詳しいから大丈夫だよ」
lines.english: “Well, I know a normal amount, anyway. It’ll be fine.”

lines.japanese: 三年生のこの時期にＲＰＧなんて、受験生なのに渡来さん余裕なんだな。僕もひとのこと言えないけど。
lines.english: An RPG at this point in our senior year. Watarai seemed remarkably carefree for someone facing entrance exams. Though I was hardly one to talk.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとー」
lines.english: “Thanks.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはにっこり微笑んで、それから、口を尖らすみたいに細い息を吹いた。
lines.english: Watarai smiled. Then she pursed her lips and breathed out a thin stream of air.

lines.japanese: 「……うん。良かった、断わられないで」
lines.english: “…Yes. I’m glad you didn’t turn me down.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「だって、たぶん断わられると思ってたもん。あー、緊張した」
lines.english: “I mean, I was pretty sure you would. Ahh, I was so nervous.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんはいつもの動じない声と表情のまま、洗面台で洗うときみたいに両手を擦りあわせた。
lines.english: Her voice and face remained as unruffled as ever, but she rubbed her hands together as though washing them at a sink.

lines.japanese: 「え、なんで。おれが断わるわけないじゃん」
lines.english: “What? Why? There’s no way I’d turn you down.”

lines.japanese: 本当に。不可解なことを言う。
lines.english: Honestly. What a baffling thing to say.

lines.japanese: 「だって羽田君、キホン人付き合いとか避けるタイプでしょ。いまは受験もあるし──」
lines.english: “Because you’re basically the type who avoids dealing with people, aren’t you? And we have entrance exams coming up—”

lines.japanese: 「え、え、ちょっと待って。なんで？　人付き合いを避けるって？　おれ、そんなこと言った？」
lines.english: “Wait, wait. What? Why? I avoid dealing with people? Did I ever say that?”

lines.japanese: 「言ってなかったっけ？　でも、見てるとカンペキそーだよね。ひとり大好きィーってカンジ」
lines.english: “Didn’t you? Well, from watching you, it’s pretty obvious. You give off this whole ‘I looove being alone’ feeling.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことは……ないと思うけど。べつに、話しかけられれば答えるし、誘われれば付いてくよ」
lines.english: “I don’t think that’s… true. If someone talks to me, I answer. If someone invites me somewhere, I go.”

lines.japanese: 「自分からは誘わないんだ」
lines.english: “But you never invite anyone yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「いや？　誘う……よ。たぶん」
lines.english: “What? I do… invite people. Probably.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー、でも羽田君、いままで下校ひとつ誘ってくれたことなかったじゃーん」
lines.english: “Oh, really? Because all this time, Haneda, you’ve never once invited me to walk home with you.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「ねー、二年半も『彼氏』なんだからいくらでも口実あったのにさー」
lines.english: “You’ve been my ‘boyfriend’ for two and a half years. You had all the excuses in the world.”

lines.japanese: 「え、いや、だって」
lines.english: “What? No, but—”

lines.japanese: 「ほら。そしたらふつー、敬遠されてるって思うよね」
lines.english: “See? Of course I’d assume you were keeping your distance from me.”

lines.japanese: 「違うよ、それ言うなら、おれより先に渡来さんが──」
lines.english: “That’s not it. If anything, you were the one who—”
“Me?”

lines.japanese: 「──渡来さんがいちばん最初に、人間きらいーとか友達いらないーみたいなこと言うから」
lines.english: “—you were the one who started off by saying you hated people and didn’t want friends and things like that.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、その中にはおれも含まれてるんだろうなって、こっちとしてはそう思うわけで……」
lines.english: “So naturally I figured that included me, too…”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「だから……気にはなってたけど、極力干渉しないであげようと思うわけで……」
lines.english: “And so… even though I wondered about you, I thought I should interfere as little as possible…”

lines.japanese: 「えええ」
lines.english: “Whaaat?”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは僕の顔の前にてのひらを置いた。
lines.english: Watarai raised a palm in front of my face.

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと待て。私のせいなのか」
lines.english: “Hold it. Are you saying this is my fault?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだと」
lines.english: “Come again?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ最初に会ったときのこと思いだしてみなよ。言ったはずだから、たしかに」
lines.english: “Think back to when we first met. You definitely said it.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは目を閉じ、腕を組み、頭を変な角度にひねった。どうやら二年前の春へさかのぼる記憶の旅に出たみたいだ。
lines.english: Watarai closed her eyes, folded her arms, and twisted her head to a peculiar angle. Apparently she had embarked upon a journey through memory, back to the spring two years before.
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: やがて何かに思いあたったらしい。閉じられた目蓋のあいだに細い皺が走った。
lines.english: At last, something seemed to come back to her. A slender crease appeared between her closed eyelids.
“…Ahh.”

lines.japanese: 「あー。あーあー。言ったかもー」
lines.english: “Ahh. Ahh, right. I might have said that.”

lines.japanese: 「かもじゃないって……」
lines.english: “There’s no ‘might’ about it…”

lines.japanese: なかなか往生際の悪いひとだ。
lines.english: She did not surrender gracefully.

lines.japanese: 「ほら。いきなりあんな風に語られたら、こっちは牽制されてると思うって」
lines.english: “See? When someone launches into a speech like that the moment you meet, you assume they’re warning you off.”
“Ahh…”

lines.japanese: 彼女は腕を組んだ直立姿勢のまま、ふらーっと真横に傾いていき、窓と廊下に架かる人間筋交いとなった。意外に愉快な動きをするひとだ。
lines.english: Still standing bolt upright with her arms folded, she began listing sideways until she became a human crossbrace between the window and the corridor. She moved in unexpectedly entertaining ways.

lines.japanese: 「……え、ちょっと待てちょっと待て」
lines.english: “…Wait. Wait just a minute.”

lines.japanese: こめかみを支点にぐりんと首を９０度曲げ、ほとんど唇が付きそうな距離のガラスに何事かをつぶやいた。
lines.english: With her temple as the pivot, she cranked her neck ninety degrees and muttered something at the glass, her lips almost touching it.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ私、嫌われてもないのにただ漫然とスルーされてたのか二年半」
lines.english: “So you didn’t dislike me. You just spent two and a half years blithely ignoring me.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あのー、渡来さん……？」
lines.english: “Um… Watarai?”

lines.japanese: なんて言ったんだろう。よく聞きとれなかった。
lines.english: What had she said? I hadn’t quite caught it.

lines.japanese: さらに彼女が溜息をつくと、遠く柳木原のビル群に白い霞がかかった。
lines.english: She heaved another sigh, and a white haze veiled the distant towers of Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: 「君ね、誘いたいなら誘いなさい」
lines.english: “Listen. If you want to invite someone, then invite them.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ」
lines.english: “Whoa.”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは出し抜けに身を起こした。例の校長先生みたいな口調で言って、堂々と腰に手を置く。
lines.english: Watarai abruptly straightened. She spoke in that principal voice of hers and planted both hands upon her hips with magnificent authority.

lines.japanese: 「男の引っ込み思案はかわいくないっ。駄目だと思っても当たって砕けるぐらいの根性はないのか！」
lines.english: “A timid man isn’t cute! Even if you think you’ll fail, haven’t you got the nerve to take a shot and crash and burn?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええっ……」
lines.english: “Wh-what…?”

lines.japanese: 僕は弱気になりかけたけど、ここで求められているのはその正反対の気質みたいだったから、なんとか彼女の目を見返して反論した。
lines.english: I nearly wilted, but apparently what she wanted from me was the exact opposite. Somehow I found the courage to meet her eyes and argue back.

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなのお互い様だろ。そっちだって、おれを誘ったことなんて一度もなかったじゃん」
lines.english: “W-well, that cuts both ways. You never invited me anywhere either. Not once.”

lines.japanese: 「お互い様ぁ？　そんなわけないでしょ、私と羽田君じゃ条件違うんだからー」
lines.english: “Cuts both ways? Of course it doesn’t. You and I are operating under completely different conditions.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ、条件って……」
lines.english: “What conditions…?”

lines.japanese: 「私、おんなのこ！」
lines.english: “I’m a girl!”

lines.japanese: そんな子供みたいな言い分を主張する彼女は、たしかに可愛らしい女の子だと思った。
lines.english: Childish as the argument was, I had to admit that she really was an endearing girl.

lines.japanese: 待ち遠しい放課後。
lines.english: Now I could hardly wait for school to end.
